shared_elements: low-relief carving on pale stone pillar/monolith
quadruped animal in profile (fox/canid-like with tail)
horizontal register or band running across the top block
row of repeated animal figures along a horizontal edge
T-shaped or capital-and-shaft pillar form set in rubble excavation context
justification: Both show the same specific scheme: a broad-headed stone pillar whose horizontal upper block carries a row of profile quadrupeds, while the vertical shaft below bears larger animals and snaking/zigzag lines, all in the same shallow, flat-topped low relief with simplified outlines and identical stone colour and weathering. The main difference is viewpoint and completeness — A is an oblique, partly buried close-up with only a few sparse animals and a bounding groove, whereas B is a frontal view with a much denser, multi-register programme including arcaded elements, a woven-looking band and bird and anthropomorphic figures absent from A.
